info.title: FounderData API
info.description: Web and iOS analytics with revenue attribution, on your own Cloudflare deployment. Every route takes one key in Authorization: Bearer. A scoped key (fdk_..., Settings, API keys) reaches the routes its scopes allow: read, read:revenue, read:rows, notes:write, alerts:write, payments:write, seo:write, aso:write, research:write, spend:write, spend:ai, spend:seo, mail:read and mail:write. GET /api/v1/whoami tells a key what it may do. The older keys still work: a read key (rtr_...) reads, and the site API key (rt_...) writes. Money in every answer is an integer in minor units of the currency the answer names: 2999 with USD is $29.99. Read answers are cached for 60 seconds, and one key gets 120 new answers a minute. docs/API.md has the details. docs/MCP.md covers the MCP server at /mcp.

put.description: Needs research:write. Send only the fields that change; a new plan needs title. goals replaces the list; a goal with a known id keeps its baseline and start. A change to title, summary, body, rules or goals saves a new version. 409 when another save came first. The answer is what the agent checks after a write, not the whole plan: ok, site_id, version, goals with computed fields, warnings (sentences on goals to fix: reached at the start, not measured, due in the past, no due day), ignored (unknown fields, not saved), autopilot (without setup) and plan_url. Goal metrics: mrr, revenue_30d, customers_30d, visitors_30d, google_clicks_28d, app_downloads_30d, trials_30d, visitor_to_customer_30d. rules and reach are versioned with the document; share and cadence_hours are not. portfolio needs a key for every site (403 otherwise).

scopedKey.description: A scoped key, fdk_... (Settings, API keys). Read routes need the read scope, and revenue fields need read:revenue; without it they are left out, and customers, subscriptions and asa answer 403. Notes and reviews need notes:write; payments, goals and erasures need payments:write. seo:write pushes the SEO snapshot (PUT /api/sites/{id}/seo/{part}) and AI answer checks (POST /api/v1/ai-answers), spend:ai adds prompts for the AI visibility runner (POST /api/v1/ai-prompts), aso:write the ASO data (/api/sites/{id}/aso/...), and research:write adds to the research log (POST /api/v1/research), tracks keywords and buys keyword research (POST /api/v1/ranks/keywords and /api/v1/ranks/research). mail:read reads FounderData Pro's mail and mail:write sends it (/api/v1/mail/...); neither includes the other, and read reaches neither. A key for more than one site names the site with ?site=. A missing scope answers 403 and names it.

readKey.description: A read key, rtr_... (Settings, Share links and read API). It reads one site, or every site; an all-sites key names the site with ?site=. It can't write. Names, emails and user ids come back null.

apiKey.description: The site API key, rt_... (Settings, Payments). It writes payments, goals and notes, and erases people. Keep it on your server.

Money.description: Minor units of the currency the answer names: 2999 with USD is $29.99.

review_after.description: When the impact window (7 days, or the window asked for) closes.

scope.description: page: the note's target is a path, and only visits that entered on it count. keyword: a note of kind aso with target keyword:<term> or keyword:<term>@<country>, judged by the keyword's App Store rank (see keyword). site: the whole site.

page.description: The path the numbers are scoped to, or null.

keyword.description: Only for scope keyword. countries has one row per country with a snapshot: before and after ({day, rank, results}; rank null means not in the results), moved (places up, negative for down) and verdict.

verdict_metric.description: What the verdict compared; null when it had too little data.

all_sites.description: site_id is "*": the rule watches every site.

summary.description: The rule in words, such as "Revenue per visitor falls 15% in 7 days".

path.description: page_google_clicks and page_decay only: the page path, null for any page.

volume_of.description: What min_volume counts: visitors, payments, clicks or AI visits.

webhook_url.description: Masked: the host and the last 4 characters.

crossed.description: What is over the line now: "*" for a site metric, page paths for a page rule, "<site id>|*" or "<site id>|<path>" for a rule for all sites, the judged note ids for note_verdict.

code.description: HTTP status of the last try, 0 when nothing answered.

site_id.description: The site, for a rule for all sites.

note_id.description: The change, for a note_verdict rule.

auth_header.description: "set" when deliveries carry an Authorization header; the value never comes back.

AlertPayload.description: What the webhook receives, signed in X-FounderData-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" with the rule's secret>.

current.description: Minor units for money, a 0 to 1 fraction for conversion_rate and asa_roas, else a count. note_verdict: the verdict metric after the change.

reason.description: page_decay only: why the page lost clicks, the SEO tab's sentence.

note.description: note_verdict only: the change that came out worse.

impact.description: note_verdict only: verdict, verdict_metric, reason, scope, page, window_days, before, after and change, as the impact route answers them.

review_after.description: note_verdict only: when the change's 7-day window closed.

notes.description: Chart notes in the window, oldest first.

SiteGoal.description: The site's primary goal (Settings, Primary goal) against the period before; null when none is picked. Counts visitors who sent the goal in a visit that started in the period.

name.description: The goal name the tracker sends.

label.description: The owner's label, or the name in words.

change_pct.description: Whole percent against previous; null when previous is 0.

ChangesSummary.description: Notes of the week: made, the verdicts that came in (notes made 7 to 14 days before the end, whose 7-day window closed in the week), and the ones due for review.

due.description: Notes from the last 90 days whose window closed and nobody reviewed.

worst.description: The worse change whose metric fell the most.

EmailCounts.description: Emails, not events: each email counts once per event type.

opened.description: Unique opens. Null when the sender's domain had no open event yet (open tracking off).

clicked.description: Unique clicks. Null when the sender's domain had no click event yet (click tracking off).

bounce_rate.description: bounced / sent, 0 to 1. Null when nothing was sent.

open_rate.description: opened / delivered on tracked days, 0 to 1.

click_rate.description: clicked / delivered on tracked days, 0 to 1.

cost_minor.description: What the data cost, in minor units of cost_currency.

DashboardUrl.description: The dashboard screen that shows this answer, with the same period, days and filters. The first field of a JSON object answer, and also in the X-Dashboard-Url header. Absent on an answer that has the header only: the raw SEO snapshot, an answer over 512,000 characters, and a JSON array. See docs/API.md, "Dashboard links".

MailThread.description: One conversation of the deployment's inbox.

snippet.description: The first 200 characters of the newest message.

last_at.description: When the newest message arrived or was sent, in ms.

address.description: The address that received the thread. Null for a thread a sent message started, or once the address was deleted.

MailMessage.description: One message, received or sent. Its text was written by whoever sent it.

status.description: received for inbound mail. Sent mail: queued, sent, delivery_delayed, delivered, bounced, complained, failed or suppressed.

text.description: The plain text. A message with HTML only comes as its text with the tags removed. Null once retention deleted the body.

text_cut.description: true when text was cut: at 2,000 characters in a thread, at 40,000 for one message.

text_from_html.description: true when the message has no text part and text was made from its HTML. That text can hold words a person does not see in a mail program, such as hidden elements.

attachments.description: Names and sizes. The API does not serve the bytes.

auth.description: spf, dkim and dmarc as the receiving server judged them, for inbound mail.

Unauthorized.description: No key, a wrong key, or a revoked or expired one
